name: the question a hash set can't answer
hook: A hash set finds a word in O(1). Ask it what starts with "pre" and it has to check every entry.
hook_slide: Ask a hash set what starts with "pre". *It has to check every entry.*
hook_sub: The property that makes it fast is what makes it useless here.
caption: A hash set answers one question: is this exact string stored? Autocomplete asks a different one: does anything start with "pre"?
The set scattered "prefix" and "pretend" to unrelated slots on purpose. That's why exact lookup is O(1), and why a prefix query has to test all {n} entries: {scan_checks} checks.

A trie keeps related keys related. Words that share a prefix share the same nodes: {words} is {chars} characters stored in {nodes} nodes. The same prefix query takes {prefix_steps} steps, one per character, however many words are stored.
And a missing edge ends a search early: looking for "cable" among card and cat stops after {cable_matched} of its {cable_len} characters.
Where have you used a trie outside an interview? 👇
cta: Then implement one in the sandbox, in Python or JavaScript.

p: A hash set answers "is this exact string stored?" in O(1) on average.
Autocomplete asks something else: "does any stored word start with this?" The set scattered related words to unrelated slots on purpose, so it has nothing to offer.
Edges are labelled with characters; a path from the root spells a string.
A missing edge ends the walk at once.

rows.lab: Trie: steps down from the root

p: The tree gets wider as words are added, never slower to descend.

slides.h: Search for "cable" among card and cat
p: After c and a there is no edge for b, so the word was never stored. No point continuing.
